assign.now: mapping the six words onto core - three real collisions found

log.msg: COLLISION 1, hard: `type` is taken. core/Page/generator/page.js:261 declares type(text){} as a page METHOD and calls it at 146/272/286. A core Page field named `type` would read that function back and stamp a class from it. The key must be `type_size` - which is already the reader-facing label (blocks.js:242 label: 'type size').

COLLISION 2: `content` is ALREADY a core Page option (a function or a string; render() Page.class.js:245, declare() 52-56, 19 call sites). Core wins outright - on a real page 'what is in the box' IS content(). The lab's eight canned renderers are demo fixtures and must not graduate. What graduates is the ninth answer: content as a URL.

COLLISION 3: `room` vs `width`. 194 declarations of `width: "..."` in the repo (large 80, small 60, full 51, fill 51, hug 5) against 2 of `room:`. width wins the key; the lab's four values join it as the page-grid half of the same axis, room: aliased in.

FREE: navigation, arrangement, surface, background are unused as Page fields or methods anywhere in framework/ or imagine/. CSS names page-nav-*, page-arr-*, page-surface-*, page-bg-*, page-type-*, page-frame all census clean; page- is core/Page's own reserved prefix (css-scopes.txt:62).

The vocabulary already crosses realms without core: /imagine/sections/sections.js:2 imports SURFACES from paging/blocks.js and /imagine/layouts/system.js:38 re-lists the same five. That is the evidence the words want to be core, not the lab's.

assign.outcome:
**The plan for making the paging lab's six words the way any page is configured — read-only, nothing under `public/` changed but this dir and one line in the day page.**

![](/framework/ai/2026-09-06/graduate-plan/summary.png)

[Six words for any page](/framework/ai/2026-09-06/graduate-plan/) — the owner's one screen: the before/after of one page file, the six words, three slices. [The plan](/framework/ai/2026-09-06/graduate-plan/plan/) — the map word by word with file and line, the seam in code, the three slices written for a cold Sonnet, the risks, the deletion list.

**The seam, in one sentence:** `Page` gains five word options plus core's existing `content` and `width`, each stamping one class and each writing nothing by default; the renderer does not graduate as a class — it splits into `Page.Frame` (a part class hung on the constructor), about 40 CSS rules in `Page.css`, and `Page.from(json)`.

**Three real collisions found by reading, not guessing.** `type` is taken — `core/Page/generator/page.js:261` declares `type(text){…}` as a page method and calls it three times, so the key is `type_size`. `content` is already a core option with 19 call sites and wins outright: on a real page, what is in the box IS `content()`, and the lab's eight canned samples stay in the lab. `room` loses to `width`, 194 declarations to 2, and is aliased in for every `page.json` already written.

**About 90 lines added to core, about 580 deleted from the lab** — five of the six deletions being a second copy of a list, which is the defect this realm has re-found in eight audits running.

**Deliberately left:** the plan is a plan — no core file was edited, per the brief's read-only fence. `arrangement`'s panel *contents* do not graduate (core ships boxes, never furniture). The url overlay stays an editor feature, as the mastermind already ruled.
